_comment: STARTER FILE for one upstream REST endpoint. Copy me into contracts/<tool_name>.json, fill every TODO, delete the _comment keys if you like (the schema allows them either way), and open a PR. Your editor validates against the schema as you type, so most mistakes surface before CI.
_comment_upstream: The platform's primary upstream is the Salla Admin API; for Salla endpoints, docs.salla.dev is the reference for method, path and scopes, and copying from it saves your reviewer a lot of back-and-forth. The format itself is not Salla-only -- any upstream the engine is configured for works, selected by binding.http.api.

interface._comment: WHAT THE TOOL IS. Maps 1:1 to the standard MCP tool shape, so any MCP client can consume it.
interface.name: TODO_snake_case_name
interface.title: TODO Human Readable Title
interface.description: TODO one sentence, at least 20 characters, saying what this returns. The agent reads this to decide whether to pick you over a sibling tool.
interface._comment_hints: LLM guidance: whenToUse is what the tool is FOR, whenNotToUse is what it is NOT for. Be concrete and name the sibling tool -- 'use get_coupon instead' is what stops the agent picking a list endpoint when the merchant named one record.
whenToUse: TODO a concrete situation where this tool is the right pick.
whenNotToUse: TODO a situation where the agent should reach for a named sibling instead.
interface._comment_annotations: MCP's core ToolAnnotations, served to clients verbatim. All four are required and the gate cross-checks them: GET must be readOnlyHint true, POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE must be false, DELETE must be destructiveHint true. annotations.title comes from `title` above.

input._comment: THE TOOL'S arguments, not the upstream's. An endpoint may accept twenty filters; expose only the few an agent should actually set. Narrowing the surface is the contract doing its job. Use friendly camelCase names here and map them to wire names under binding.http.parameters.
input._comment_forbidden: Optional. Argument names a caller must never be able to supply.

response._comment: Describe what is INSIDE the envelope's data. Never model the {status, success, data} wrapper -- the engine unwraps it before anyone sees it.
response._comment_ui: Optional render hint. {braces} interpolate fields from the response.

binding._comment: WHERE IT CALLS. Note there is no baseUrl: the engine owns each upstream's host and credentials, so a contract cannot pin production. Use type 'none' with a builtin:// handler instead if this tool computes rather than fetches.

http._comment_api: Which configured upstream to call. 'salla' is the default and the platform's primary upstream; a new value needs the engine configured for it first.
http._comment_traceability: Optional but strongly recommended: summary and docsUrl let a reviewer check this contract against its source without guessing which endpoint you meant.
http.summary: TODO the upstream's own summary for this endpoint
http._comment_auth: No secret is named here. The engine resolves the upstream credential at call time -- for Salla, the installing merchant's OAuth token. You only declare which scopes it must carry, in the <domain>.read / <domain>.read_write convention. Ask for the narrowest that works: a read-only tool must use .read, and the schema enforces it.
http._comment_parameters: How the tool's arguments become the request. `name` is the wire name, `from` is the tool argument feeding it. Omit `from` when they match.

path.name: TODO_id
path.description: Every {placeholder} in `path` needs an entry here.

query.name: page
query.description: Salla-style upstreams paginate with `page`. Expose it whenever the endpoint returns a list.

parameters._comment_body: For POST/PUT/PATCH. mode 'none' sends no body, 'passthrough' sends every argument not consumed by path or query, 'mapped' sends only the fields you list.

http._comment_response: Salla-style envelopes wrap everything in {status, success, data}, plus a pagination object on lists. This tells the engine what to unwrap.

validation._comment: Optional. These regexes are compiled into the generated code as real guards, so a bad argument fails locally instead of costing a round trip and an upstream 422.

rules.message: TODO_field must be a numeric id

_comment_dependencies: Other contracts this tool depends on, e.g. [{"contract": "list_coupons", "reason": "coupon ids come from list_coupons"}]. Documentation for the reviewer and the agent; the POC engine does not resolve or order these yet.

governance._comment: HOW IT IS ALLOWED TO RUN. This layer is ours; MCP leaves it open. The schema cross-checks it against interface.annotations and the HTTP method, so policy cannot quietly disagree with declared behavior.
governance._comment_execution: 'direct' runs immediately. 'propose-apply' returns a proposal and waits for a human; it requires humanApproval 'required'.
governance._comment_caching: Only read-only tools may be cacheable, and a cacheable tool must set a ttlSeconds or its result never expires. keyBy picks which arguments form the cache key -- omit it to key on all of them.
